items.claim: The title-plus-motto complex Prov.1.1-Prov.1.7 is a byte-grounded editorial unit closing on the petuchah at 1.7.
items.evidence: mishle verse-initial at 1.1 (Phase-0 fact, 2/915 book-wide with 10.1) opens the title; the infinitive-construct chain recurs verse-initial at 1.2 (לָדַ֣עַת), 1.3 (לָ֭קַחַת), 1.4 (לָתֵ֣ת) and 1.6 (לְהָבִ֣ין), correctly broken once by the finite hearer clause at 1.5 (יִשְׁמַ֣ע, imperfect, not infinitive) -- confirmed byte tier by collate.py at all four sites. The word pair חָכְמָ֥ה וּ֝מוּסָ֗ר closing 1.7 is disclosed as skeleton tier (unpointed) as required and is confirmed by sweep.py --skel to recur at 1.2/1.7 (plus one unrelated hit at 23.23, not claimed as unique) -- a real bracket, not a fabricated one. Petuchah at 1.7 confirmed single-witness against pmarks_Prov.json.

items.claim: The exordium Prov.1.8-Prov.1.9 is correctly bounded between the 1.7 petuchah and the fresh vocative-plus-conditional at 1.10.
items.evidence: Imperative-plus-vocative שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי confirmed byte tier at 1.8; the rationale clause at 1.9 passes the WEB verbatim-quote check clean; the vocative-plus-conditional בְּנִ֡י אִם confirmed byte tier at 1.10 is a distinct construction (protasis, not bare imperative), a real tier-1 seam. boundary_evidence_refs correctly carries the bare 1.19 mention from rejected_alternative (check_refs_mirror clean).

items.claim: The quoted-invitation unit Prov.1.10-Prov.1.14 is correctly bounded by the register shift back to 2ms address at 1.15.
items.evidence: Conditional-protasis chain confirmed byte tier: בְּנִ֡י אִם יְפַתּ֥וּךָ (1.10) and אִם יֹאמְרוּ֮ (1.11). The quoted invitation is carried in 1cp cohortative/volitive verb forms through 1.11-1.14 (e.g. נֶאֶרְבָ֥ה, נְמַלֵּ֖א), a grammatical fact independent of the WEB rendering, not merely an English quotation-mark artifact. Register reverts to 2ms address at 1.15 (בְּנִ֗י אַל תֵּלֵ֣ךְ), a genuine seam. The 1.14 WEB quote passes the campaign's punctuation-normalized verbatim check clean (check_web_quotes.py GREEN).

items.claim: The application unit Prov.1.15-Prov.1.19 is correctly bounded, closing on the 1.19 petuchah.
items.evidence: Vocative-plus-prohibition בְּנִ֗י אַל תֵּלֵ֣ךְ confirmed byte tier at 1.15. The closing clause 1.19 opens with the generalizing particle כֵּ֗ן ("so/thus"), consistent with the row's "gnomic summary" label; petuchah at 1.19 confirmed single-witness against pmarks_Prov.json. boundary_evidence_refs correctly range-cites 1.11-1.14 for the quoted scenario being applied.

items.claim: The poem Prov.1.20-Prov.1.33 is soundly bracketed by the 1.19/1.33 petuchahs, but the row's claim that Wisdom's "first-person reproach" begins at 1.22 outruns the Hebrew grammar at that verse.
items.evidence: 1.22's own verbs are 2nd/3rd person, not 1st person: תְּֽאֵהֲב֫וּ ("you(pl) will love", 2mp), חָמְד֣וּ ("they desired", 3cp), יִשְׂנְאוּ ("they hate", 3cp). The first genuine 1st-person self-reference verbs are אַבִּ֣יעָה ("I will pour out") and אוֹדִ֖יעָה ("I will make known") at 1.23, one verse later. The row's "beginning Prov.1.22" claim leans on WEB's own opening curly-quote placement at 1.22 (a translation/editorial signal) rather than the Hebrew person-morphology at that exact verse, which does not turn first-person until 1.23 -- a translation-dependent argument the OL lens is charged to contest. The unit's outer boundary is unaffected: the petuchahs at 1.19 and 1.33 (both confirmed single-witness) and the ketiv/qere at 1.27 (confirmed single-witness) all check out.

items.claim: Chapter 2 (Prov.2.1-Prov.2.22) is correctly kept as one row: a single long sentence closing on the 2.22 petuchah.
items.evidence: The chapter's one vocative בְּ֭נִי אִם תִּקַּ֣ח is confirmed byte tier at 2.1 and confirmed absent elsewhere in the chapter by direct inspection of 2.2-2.22. The claimed byte-identical twin apodosis opener אָ֗ז תָּ֭בִין is confirmed byte-identical at both 2.5 and 2.9 (collate.py, both byte tier; strings equal=True). The claimed byte-identical twin purpose infinitive לְ֭הַצִּ֣ילְךָ is confirmed byte-identical at both 2.12 and 2.16 (strings equal=True). The concluding לְמַ֗עַן is confirmed byte tier at 2.20. Petuchah at 1.33 (preceding) and 2.22 (closing) and ketiv/qere at 2.7 and 2.8 all confirmed single-witness against pmarks_Prov.json; check_marks.py and citation_sweep.py both GREEN over this row.

items.claim: The row's divine-name contrast between Prov.3.1-Prov.3.4 and the couplets from 3.5 is built on a fabricated Hebrew claim, and its device-inventory figure is stale.
items.evidence: The rationale and rejected_alternative both assert the couplets "beginning at 3.5 each name אֶל (oshb:Prov.3.5) directly, while neither couplet in 3.1-3.4 does" -- but אֶל (segol, "to/toward") is a preposition, not the divine name, and word-bound checking of the pointed text shows it occurs ONLY in 3.5 (twice: בְּטַ֣ח אֶל יְ֭הוָה ... וְאֶל בִּֽ֝ינָתְךָ֗), nowhere else in 3.1-3.12. It is never claimed to recur at 3.7/3.9/3.11/3.12 by the row's own citations (every instance is anchored to oshb:Prov.3.5), only in prose -- and that prose extension is false: 3.7 opens with אַל (patach, "don't" -- a different word, same bare skeleton) before אֶת (object marker) precedes יְ֝הוָ֗ה; 3.9 has אֶת (object marker) before יְ֭הוָה; 3.11 opens מוּסַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה (construct, no particle at all) then אַל/וְאַל (twice "don't"); 3.12 has אֶ֥ת before יְהוָ֣ה. A book-wide skeleton sweep for the two letters aleph-lamed returns 109 verses -- exactly the contained-substring/homograph trap the toolkit catalogs, blending this preposition with the unrelated negative particle and the God-word's first two letters -- and check_universals.py independently flags this same "each name" clause as an undocumented universal. The word that actually recurs once each at 3.5/3.7/3.9/3.11/3.12 is יְ֭הוָה itself, which the row never quotes; 3.1-3.4 does carry a different God-word once (אֱלֹהִ֣ים at 3.4), so a real contrast exists but is not the one argued. Separately, the row cites "bni_address inventory: 17 tokens book-wide" -- prov_device_inventory.json's bni_address object gives count 22 (E-1 corrected); 17 is the stale pre-correction figure this cycle's own materials flag by name.

items.claim: The row's core naming-density argument for Prov.3.5-Prov.3.12 as one unit, and for reading the internal 3.10 petuchah as non-boundary, rests on the same fabricated Hebrew claim as P02-001.
items.evidence: "אֶל (oshb:Prov.3.5) named in 3.5, 3.7, 3.9, 3.11, 3.12 (5 tokens across the row's 8 verses)" is false at the word-bound pointed tier: אֶל (segol, "to/toward") occurs only in 3.5 (twice); 3.7 and 3.11 instead carry אַל/אַל (patach, "don't" -- a different word sharing only the bare skeleton); 3.9 and 3.12 carry אֶת/אֶ֥ת (the direct-object marker, spelled with tav, not lamed) -- neither is the cited preposition. The word genuinely recurring once each at 3.5/3.7/3.9/3.11/3.12 is יְ֭הוָה, never quoted by the row. The same false premise underwrites the claim that "both" couplets flanking the internal petuchah after 3.10 (confirmed single-witness) "name אֶל" and so the mark falls mid-unit rather than at an edge -- the honor couplet (3.9-3.10) and the discipline couplet (3.11-3.12) in fact contain no instance of אֶל at all (see the object-marker and negative-particle tokens above), so that specific cohesion argument needs to be re-argued from the actual יְ֭הוָה-naming pattern rather than from אֶל.
